# qweek-ui — URL → live-previewed HTML clone (Design)

**Date:** 2026-06-21
**Status:** Approved design, pre-implementation
**Goal:** Paste a website URL → get a 1:1, self-contained HTML clone of its homepage in under 5 minutes, rendered progressively into a live preview, generated by Claude running on the user's Max subscription via the `claude` CLI (no API key / no metered billing).

Inspired by aidesigner.ai/website-cloner. This is a clean, new build — it deliberately does **not** reuse the existing `nextjs-clone` ShopKit pipeline on this machine.

---

## 1. Scope

### In scope (v1)
- Single input: a URL.
- Capture the **homepage at desktop width (1440px)** only.
- Output: **one self-contained `.html` file** using **Tailwind via CDN**, with real scraped image URLs and real copy.
- Live UX: stream pipeline stages + Claude's reasoning ("Thought Process"), and **progressively render completed sections into a live iframe** — earlier sections stay visible while later ones stream in.
- Result actions: **View/copy code**, **Download .html**, **Open in new tab**.

### Out of scope (v1 — explicit YAGNI)
- Mobile / responsive capture and output.
- Multi-page crawl.
- In-place visual editor.
- React / Next component output (planned enhancement later).
- Auth, persistence, database, job history.
- Automatic retry (manual re-generate is a later add).

---

## 2. Architecture

Next.js (App Router) app at `/Users/aniqhaider/projects/qweek-ui`.

```
Browser (Next.js client)
   │  POST /api/clone {url}            → validates URL, creates jobId, kicks off pipeline
   │  GET  /api/clone/stream?jobId=…   → Server-Sent Events stream
   ▼
API routes  ── orchestrate ──►  lib/capture.ts   (Playwright: screenshot tiles)
                                lib/scrape.ts     (assets / text / design tokens)
                                lib/prompt.ts     (build the generation prompt)
                                lib/generate.ts   (spawn `claude` CLI, parse stream)
```

Each `lib/*` module has a single responsibility, a plain typed interface, and is independently testable.

### Modules

**`lib/capture.ts`**
- Input: `url`, `jobId`.
- Launch Chromium (Playwright) at viewport 1440×900.
- Navigate (`networkidle`, with timeout), auto-scroll top→bottom to trigger lazy-loaded images, scroll back to top.
- Take a full-page screenshot, then slice it into vertical tiles of ~1400px tall (better vision fidelity than one very tall image).
- Returns: `{ tiles: string[] /* file paths */, pageHeight: number }`.
- Reuses the same Playwright `page` instance with `scrape.ts` (one browser session).

**`lib/scrape.ts`**
- Runs in the same page context (via `page.evaluate`).
- Extracts:
  - absolute `<img>` `src` + `alt`,
  - CSS `background-image` URLs,
  - the logo (best-effort: header img / `[class*=logo]`),
  - all visible text content,
  - design tokens: dominant colors and `font-family` values from computed styles.
- Returns a structured `ScrapeResult` JSON.
- Purpose: gives Claude **real** asset URLs and copy so the clone shows actual product photos and exact text, not placeholders.

**`lib/prompt.ts`**
- Input: `ScrapeResult`, `url`.
- Builds the instruction text: clone this page as ONE self-contained HTML file; Tailwind via CDN; use the provided real asset URLs and text; desktop layout.
- **Mandates delimited output markers** so the stream can be split into sections:
  ```
  <!--HEAD-->… tailwind cdn <script>, fonts, tailwind.config …<!--/HEAD-->
  <!--SECTION:hero-->…<!--/SECTION-->
  <!--SECTION:categories-->…<!--/SECTION-->
  … (one SECTION block per visual section, in document order) …
  ```
- Output of the model is the file content itself (HEAD + ordered SECTION blocks), nothing else.

**`lib/generate.ts`**
- Spawns:
  ```
  claude -p \
    --output-format stream-json \
    --input-format stream-json \
    --include-partial-messages \
    --verbose \
    --model claude-opus-4-8 \
    --permission-mode bypassPermissions
  ```
  (Model is a single swappable constant: `GEN_MODEL`.)
- Sends **one user message** (as a stream-json line) containing the prompt text **+ screenshot tiles as base64 `image` content blocks**.
- **Fallback** if base64 image input proves unreliable in the CLI: write tiles to the job temp dir and instruct Claude to `Read` them, adding `--allowedTools Read`. (To be verified during implementation; primary path is base64 blocks.)
- Parses streamed JSON events; converts assistant text deltas into the app's own event types (below).

---

## 3. SSE event contract

Emitted by `/api/clone/stream` to the client:

| event     | payload                         | meaning |
|-----------|---------------------------------|---------|
| `stage`   | `{ stage: 'capturing'\|'scraping'\|'generating' }` | pipeline progress |
| `thought` | `{ text: string }`              | reasoning delta → Thought Process panel |
| `head`    | `{ html: string }`              | the HEAD block completed |
| `section` | `{ name: string, html: string }`| a SECTION block completed |
| `done`    | `{ fullHtml: string }`          | full assembled file |
| `error`   | `{ message: string }`           | fatal error |

`generate.ts` maintains a small parser that scans the accumulating assistant text for closed `<!--HEAD-->…<!--/HEAD-->` and `<!--SECTION:x-->…<!--/SECTION-->` blocks and emits `head` / `section` exactly once per block.

---

## 4. Progressive live preview (client)

- The result view holds an `<iframe srcdoc={…}>`.
- Client state: `head: string`, `sections: {name, html}[]`.
- On `head`: store it.
- On `section`: append to `sections`, then rebuild and re-set `srcdoc`:
  ```html
  <!doctype html><html><head>{head}</head><body>{sections joined}</body></html>
  ```
  Tailwind CDN re-runs on each `srcdoc` reload and styles the accumulated DOM. Earlier sections remain visible; new sections appear below — the requested behavior.
- On `done`: final `fullHtml` becomes the canonical file for download / copy / open-in-tab.

A left/side panel shows `stage` + streamed `thought` text (monospace, auto-scroll), mirroring aidesigner's Thought Process.

---

## 5. UI

- **Landing screen:** centered headline, a single URL input with a Clone button (disabled→"Cloning…" while running). Minimal, aidesigner-like.
- **Clone screen:** two-pane — Thought Process / stages on the left, live iframe preview on the right. Result actions appear on `done`: View/copy code (code drawer), Download .html, Open in new tab.

---

## 6. Error handling

- Invalid/empty URL → 400 from `POST /api/clone`, inline UI message.
- Playwright nav timeout / crash → `error` event, message shown, pipeline stops.
- `claude` CLI non-zero exit or unparseable stream → `error` event.
- Per-job temp dir at `os.tmpdir()/qweek-ui/<jobId>`; cleaned after `done`/`error`.

---

## 7. Dependencies & setup

- App: `next`, `react`, `react-dom`, `tailwindcss` (for qweek-ui's own UI), `playwright`.
- `npx playwright install chromium` (one-time).
- `claude` CLI: already installed (v2.1.185) and authed on the Max subscription.
- Node 25 / Bun 1.3.9 available; use **bun** for package management per environment convention.

---

## 8. Performance / 5-minute budget

- Capture (launch + nav + scroll + screenshot + scrape): ~10–30s.
- Generation (Opus 4.8, single homepage HTML): ~1–4 min.
- Total target: under 5 minutes. Tiling keeps vision fidelity high without an enormous single image; base64 input avoids agentic Read round-trips.

---

## 9. Risks / to verify in implementation

1. **Base64 image blocks over `--input-format stream-json`** — confirm the installed CLI accepts `image` content blocks; if not, switch to the disk-`Read` fallback.
2. **Tailwind CDN re-processing on every `srcdoc` reset** — if flicker is bad, switch to surgical DOM injection via `postMessage` instead of full `srcdoc` rebuilds.
3. **Very long pages** — extreme tile counts could bloat the prompt; cap tile count (e.g. first N) if needed and note the cap.
4. **CORS/asset hotlinking** — some scraped image URLs may block hotlinking; acceptable for v1 (visual approximation), note in UI if many images fail.
